subject: Exhibition game (basketball)
query: what is an exhibition game in basketball
title: What is an exhibition game in basketball? A tune-up that doesn't count
answer: An exhibition game in basketball is a preseason game played for practice, not for the standings. It does not count toward a team's official win-loss record, and players' points and rebounds do not go into their official season statistics. College teams use exhibitions in late October and early November to test lineups before the regular season.
in_the_news: Every fall, top college programs open with exhibitions just before the season starts, so fans see a final score and wonder whether the result matters. It does not.
body:
Exhibitions look like real games: referees, a full 40 minutes in college, a crowd and often a TV or streaming broadcast. Coaches treat them as dress rehearsals. They play deep into the bench, try new rotations and check how freshmen and transfers handle a real crowd.

In NCAA Division I men's basketball, each team may play up to two preseason exhibition games. Starting with the 2025-26 season, the NCAA eased the rules: exhibitions no longer need a special waiver, teams can play other four-year schools, including Division I teams, and schools no longer have to give the proceeds to charity. That is why big-name matchups between major programs now show up on the October schedule.

Scrimmages are a separate thing. A scrimmage is a practice game against another team, and under the new rules it no longer has to be closed to the public. In the NBA the equivalent is the preseason: each team plays a handful of games in October that also do not count toward the regular-season record.

faq.q: Do exhibition games count in college basketball
faq.a: No. Exhibition results are not part of a team's official win-loss record, and they do not count toward NCAA Tournament selection metrics.

faq.q: Do player stats count in an exhibition game
faq.a: No. Points, rebounds and other numbers from exhibitions are not added to a player's official season or career statistics.

faq.q: How many exhibition games can a college basketball team play
faq.a: Division I men's teams may play up to two preseason exhibition games. Since the 2025-26 season, those games can be against other four-year schools, including Division I teams.

faq.q: What is the difference between an exhibition and a scrimmage
faq.a: An exhibition is a public game with a posted score. A scrimmage is a practice game between two teams; since 2025-26 it no longer has to be closed to the public.
